value_stream.name: Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) & Integrated Business Planning

fields.Participants: S&OP Lead, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Marketing (links to VS-14), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-101), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Logistics (links to VS-06/VS-110), Sourcing/Import (links to VS-122/VS-87), Strategy (links to VS-33), Commodity (links to VS-106)
fields.Trigger: Annual planning cycle (links to VS-33.1); executive mandate
fields.Volume: 1 enterprise S&OP/IBP process (18–24 month rolling horizon, per step 1)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review → supply review → pre-S&OP → exec S&OP → plan publication" (replaces manual Step 1).
Controls: - operational: consensus cycle and single-number governance; operational: fixed calendar and exec sponsorship
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-single-number risk**: Each function brings its own forecast; mitigated by consensus cycle and single-number governance
- **Cadence-drift risk**: Cycle slips under operational pressure; mitigated by fixed calendar and exec sponsorship
System Touchpoints: - S&OP/IBP platform; supply planning (links to VS-02); merchandise financial planning (links to VS-101); corporate planning (links to VS-33); logistics (links to VS-06/VS-110); sourcing (links to VS-122/VS-87)
Time Estimate: - 2–3 weeks annual design + monthly cycle facilitation

steps.activity: S&OP/Demand-Supply design the S&OP/IBP operating model: horizon (18–24 month rolling), granularity (category/region/SKU-family monthly → key-SKU weekly), the five-step monthly cycle (demand review → supply review → pre-S&OP → exec S&OP → plan publication), product-treatment segments (A/B/C links to profile §6.6), and KPIs (forecast accuracy, plan adherence, service level, inventory turns)

S&OP establish governance: S&OP chair (typically Demand-Supply Planning leader), executive sponsor (COO), the demand-consensus participants (Sales/Marketing/Merchandising/Finance/Supply), decision rights, escalation path, and integration to corporate planning (links to VS-33) and merchandise financial planning (links to VS-101)
COO/Executive ratify the cadence, calendar (monthly cycle aligned to financial close), and the single-number principle (one agreed plan), and cascade to functions

fields.Participants: Demand Planning, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Insights (links to VS-28.1), IT (links to VS-27/VS-28), Consumer Insights (links to VS-44)
fields.Volume: ~35,000 active SKUs × 200 stores/4 DCs; ~55,000 SKU master

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generate the statistical baseline forecast per SKU/region" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "Demand Planning segment SKUs by treatment" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Demand Planning publish the baseline to the consensus review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: monthly retrain and bias tracking (links to W3911); operational: ABC segmentation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Model-staleness risk**: Out-of-date models mis-forecast seasonal shifts; mitigated by monthly retrain and bias tracking (links to W3911)
- **Granularity-cost risk**: Forecasting all 35K SKUs at store-level is costly; mitigated by ABC segmentation
System Touchpoints: - Forecasting/ML platform (links to VS-30.2); sales history (links to VS-08/VS-28); pricing (links to VS-01.2); seasonal (links to VS-64/VS-69); store openings (links to VS-37); insights (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Demand Planning/Data Science generate the statistical baseline forecast per SKU/region: time-series models (seasonal, trend, Croston for slow-movers), hierarchical reconciliation (category → SKU, region → store), outlier cleansing, and incorporate the seasonal calendar (links to profile §13.2 and VS-64)

Demand Planning segment SKUs by treatment (A-items statistical + override; B-items statistical; C-items aggregate/profile) to balance effort, and incorporate causal factors (price links to VS-01.2, weather/typhoon links to VS-69, holidays, store openings links to VS-37)
Demand Planning publish the baseline to the consensus review (links to W3907) with confidence intervals, model lineage, and exceptions for review

fields.Participants: S&OP Lead, Merchandising/Category (links to VS-01), Sales/Trade (links to VS-11/VS-107), Marketing (links to VS-14), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-101), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Supply (links to VS-02), Ecommerce (links to VS-10)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "S&OP facilitate the demand-consensus meeting" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "accountability and feedback to model learning" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: override tracking and accountability; operational: structured override and intelligence input
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bias risk**: Sales over-forecasts to secure supply, Finance under-forecasts to protect margin; mitigated by override tracking and accountability
- **Anchor risk**: Baseline over-influences consensus; mitigated by structured override and intelligence input
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; promotions (links to VS-58/VS-14); key account (links to VS-107); trade pro (links to VS-43); ecommerce (links to VS-10); finance (links to VS-17.4/VS-101)

steps.activity: S&OP facilitate the demand-consensus meeting: review baseline (links to W3906), incorporate sales/marketing intelligence (promotions links to VS-58/VS-14, key-account pipeline links to VS-107, trade-pro activity links to VS-43, ecommerce trends links to VS-10), and reconcile divergent views into one unconstrained demand plan
Functions provide structured demand overrides with justification and ownership (override reason codes, confidence), tracked for accountability and feedback to model learning (links to W3911)
S&OP publish the unconstrained consensus demand plan (volume by category/region/SKU-family over the horizon) for the supply review (links to W3913) and financial reconciliation (links to W3921)

fields.Participants: Demand Planning, Merchandising/Category (links to VS-01), Supply (links to VS-02), Sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122), Marketing (links to VS-14), Quality (links to VS-31), Store Ops/Space (links to VS-55/VS-07), Insights (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: NPI (links to VS-01.1); SKU lifecycle event
fields.Volume: ~5–8% annual SKU growth (~1,500–2,500 new SKUs/yr, the corpus canon); seasonal intros

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-forecast of "forecast new-product demand using like-item modeling, market/competitive…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track NPI forecast vs actual and feed launch-learning back into like-item models" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: like-item modeling and phase-in ramp; operational: burn plan and substitutes
Pain Points / Risks: - **NPI-overstock risk**: Optimistic NPI forecast leaves excess; mitigated by like-item modeling and phase-in ramp
- **Phase-out-leftover risk**: Poor sell-down leaves obsolete stock; mitigated by burn plan and substitutes
System Touchpoints: - NPI/assortment (links to VS-01.1); competitive intel (links to VS-57); space/allocation (links to VS-55); seasonal clearance (links to VS-64); obsolete inventory (links to VS-05.3); quality (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: Demand Planning/Merchandising forecast new-product demand using like-item modeling, market/competitive intelligence (links to VS-57), and launch curves; set initial allocation/store coverage (links to VS-01.1/VS-55) and the phase-in ramp over the horizon

Demand Planning/Merchandising manage phase-out/end-of-life for discontinuing SKUs (links to VS-64 seasonal clearance): sell-down plan, inventory-burn target, substitute/cross-sell mapping, and final clearance (links to VS-05.3/VS-64) to avoid obsolete stock
Demand Planning track NPI forecast vs actual and feed launch-learning back into like-item models (links to W3911), and refresh the active-SKU base for the next cycle

fields.Participants: Demand Planning, Marketing (links to VS-14/VS-58), Merchandising (links to VS-01.2), Supply (links to VS-02), Finance (links to VS-101/VS-128), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Insights (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Promo plan (links to VS-14/VS-58); event calendar
fields.Volume: ~6 major sales/yr + monthly hot deals + seasonal events

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow orchestration of "coordinate pre-build/inbound with Supply/Sourcing" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "post-promo lift vs forecast" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: halo/cannibalization modeling; operational: forward-buy adjustment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cannibalization-blind risk**: Promo lifts one SKU but cannibalizes another; mitigated by halo/cannibalization modeling
- **Pull-forward risk**: Promo borrows from future demand; mitigated by forward-buy adjustment
System Touchpoints: - Promo/coupon (links to VS-58); marketing (links to VS-14); pricing (links to VS-01.2); supply (links to VS-02); trade promo (links to VS-128); margin (links to VS-101); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Demand Planning/Marketing model promo lift: base vs incremental, halo (links to VS-01 category), cannibalization, and forward-buy/pull-forward effect, using historical promo performance (links to VS-14.1/VS-58) and competitive context (links to VS-57)

Demand Planning size the promo demand into the consensus plan (links to W3907), coordinate pre-build/inbound with Supply/Sourcing (links to VS-02/VS-122), and align to the trade-promotion/MD budget (links to VS-128/VS-101)
Demand Planning/Insights measure post-promo lift vs forecast (links to W3911/VS-128 post-event analysis), capture learning for the next promo model, and flag margin-erosion (links to VS-101)

fields.Participants: Demand Planning, Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Ecommerce (links to VS-10), Logistics (links to VS-06), Insights (links to VS-28.1), Disaster Response (links to VS-69)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Demand Planning translate sensed shifts into short-cycle forecast adjustments" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor sensing-accuracy and avoid over-reaction" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: thresholds and exception handling; operational: longer-horizon sensing for imports
Pain Points / Risks: - **Plan-nervousness risk**: Over-reacting to short-term signals destabilizes the plan and vendor orders; mitigated by thresholds and exception handling
- **Signal-lag risk**: Late signals miss the response window for import items (45–90 day lead — links to VS-122); mitigated by longer-horizon sensing for imports
System Touchpoints: - POS/events (links to VS-08); ecommerce (links to VS-10); typhoon/disaster (links to VS-69); competitive (links to VS-57); supply expedites (links to VS-02/VS-06/VS-74); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Demand Planning sense near-term demand shifts from real-time signals: POS velocity (links to VS-08), ecommerce trend (links to VS-10), weather/typhoon (links to VS-69 — flood-control spikes), local events/construction booms, and competitor stock-outs (links to VS-57)

Demand Planning translate sensed shifts into short-cycle forecast adjustments (0–4 week horizon) for A-items and event-driven categories, and trigger expedite/rebalancing with Supply/Logistics (links to VS-02/VS-06/VS-74)
Demand Planning monitor sensing-accuracy and avoid over-reaction (nervousness), with thresholds for when to adjust vs hold the plan (links to W3911)

fields.Participants: Demand Planning, Insights (links to VS-28.1), Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Supply (links to VS-02), Finance (links to VS-17.4), S&OP Lead

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-forecast of "Demand Planning/Insights measure forecast accuracy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify persistent bias" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track improvement vs the accuracy target" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: bias tracking and correction; operational: multi-metric scorecard
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unmeasured-bias risk**: Persistent forecast bias distorts the plan and inventory; mitigated by bias tracking and correction
- **Gaming risk**: Forecasters game accuracy metrics; mitigated by multi-metric scorecard
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-28.1); model platform (links to VS-30.2); sales history (links to VS-08/VS-28); S&OP scorecard (links to W3925)

steps.activity: Demand Planning/Insights measure forecast accuracy (MAPE/WMAPE/Bias) by category/region/SKU-family and horizon, segmented by treatment (A/B/C), source (statistical vs override), and event vs steady-state

Demand Planning identify persistent bias (over/under) by forecaster/category, run root-cause (model gap, override bias, regime change), and apply correction (model retrain, override coaching, parameter tuning — links to VS-30.2)
Demand Planning publish the forecast-accuracy scorecard to the S&OP cycle (links to W3919/W3925) and track improvement vs the accuracy target

fields.Participants: S&OP Lead, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-101), Supply (links to VS-02), Marketing (links to VS-14), Strategy (links to VS-33), Trade (links to VS-11/VS-107)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "S&OP compare the unconstrained consensus demand" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "S&OP identify gap-closing levers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documented options and financial impact" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-610 (ensure controlled execution — S&OP/IBP Framework, Demand Consensus & Forecasting (PA-127.1).)
- operational: explicit gap-closing options and exec decision; operational: margin-aware gap-closing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Gap-acceptance risk**: Gaps accepted without action erode targets; mitigated by explicit gap-closing options and exec decision
- **Demand-shape-overuse risk**: Promo/pricing used to close gaps erodes margin (links to VS-101); mitigated by margin-aware gap-closing
System Touchpoints: - S&OP platform; merchandise financial plan (links to VS-101); corporate targets (links to VS-33); pricing (links to VS-01.2); sourcing (links to VS-122); key account (links to VS-107)

steps.activity: S&OP compare the unconstrained consensus demand (links to W3907) to financial/strategic targets (revenue/margin links to VS-101/VS-33, service level, turn target links to profile §12.3) and quantify the gap

S&OP identify gap-closing levers: demand-shaping (promo links to W3909, pricing links to VS-01.2), supply acceleration (sourcing links to VS-122, expedites), inventory re-balancing (links to VS-02), and trade/key-account pipeline (links to VS-107)
S&OP escalate unresolvable gaps to pre-S&OP/exec S&OP (links to W3916/W3919) for decision (accept gap, invest, re-sequence), with documented options and financial impact
